key_insight: Prompt tuning failures in CLIP-style VLMs are largely caused by shifts in the visual encoder's foreground attention; FVG-PT adaptively extracts and aligns foreground attention to guide prompt updates, stabilizing and improving downstream performance.
problem_solved: Existing prompt tuning methods ignore internal attention shifts in the visual encoder, leading to inconsistent or degraded predictions when foreground attention drifts during adaptation; this work addresses unstable transfer and poor robustness caused by unaligned visual attention.
method: Diagnose attention shift: analyze how foreground attention maps change during prompt tuning and correlate shifts with prediction errors.
Foreground View-Guided module: extract image-specific foreground attention views and use them to condition prompt representations (attention-guided prompt generation or re-weighting).
Adaptive alignment and loss: incorporate an attention-alignment objective and a lightweight, plug-and-play prompt adapter that adjusts prompts per image or batch to preserve correct foreground focus.
impact: FVG-PT improves transfer accuracy, robustness, and interpretability of CLIP-based prompt tuning with minimal overhead, making prompt adaptation more reliable for real-world downstream tasks and low-data regimes.
visual_elements: Before/after attention heatmaps showing foreground attention drift and correction by FVG-PT

paper_title: FVG-PT: Adaptive Foreground View-Guided Prompt Tuning for Vision-Language Models
paper_authors: Haoyang Li, Liang Wang, Siyu Zhou, Jiacheng Sun, Jing Jiang
